newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude sees light Mideast grades weaken.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude sees light Mideast grades weaken.

text.p: Trading on light Mideast crudes was picking up Wednesday, but levels were under pressure as refinery stocks of middle distillates remained high.
A July Qatar Land was done at QGPC -28 cents to a major.
There were rumours of various July Murban deals done, but traders said the only cargo sold this week was by a shosha.
But the seller would not confirm the price, heard to be ADNOC -26.5.
Availabilities of June supplies were also impacting buyer's ideas of the July market. At least one June Lower Zakum was still on offer, sources said.
But rumours that an Abu Dhabi equity producer had recently sold June Murban to Africa and June Lower Zakum and Murban cargoes to a major, at Dubai related levels, were denied.
The seller said it had committed all its June supplies a week ago.
In the Asian crude market, Duri was holding its strength, with a June parcel sold by a western trader at ICP +30.
This was the first Duri done for some days and was a sharp contrast to May trades which were done at discounts.
"The May Duri market was bad, but the June situation is drastically different," one trader said.

But unsold June supplies were keeping the light crude market deppressed. There was still a parcel of June Thevenard Island, which will probably be submitted into the Bangchak tender, as few other buyers were seen. June Harriet was also available.
A cargo of end June North West Shelf condensate held by a major was finally sold early this week.
Exact details of the trade were unclear. The cargo was heard going to the U.S. for petrochemical use and was done partly at fixed price and partly on a WTI basis.
The price equates to Tapis APPI -$1.50, said the seller.
A Dai Hung tender for end June/early July closes today.
